Author: Dinesh Kumar Singh
Bench: Dinesh Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Court No. - 13
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 337 of 2009
Revisionist :- Jagdish Prasad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Revisionist :- Pradeep Shukla
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J. 
1.

The present revision is directed against the judgement and order dated 29.06.2009 passed by the V-Additional District Judge, Sultanpur in Criminal Appeal No.27 of 2005, which was preferred against the judgement and order dated 05.5.2005 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sultanpur in Criminal Case No.1245 of 2002, whereby convicting the revisionist under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (for short 'the Act'), and sentencing him to undergo six months rigorous imprisonment with a fine of Rs.1,000/- and in event of non-payment of fine, one month's additional sentence.
2. Aggrieved by the aforesaid judgement and order of the trial court, the revisionist filed an appeal before the Additional Sessions Judge.
However, the appeal has been dismissed and the judgment and order passed by the trial court has been upheld by the impugned order.

sentences.text:
The facts of the case are that on 24.07.2001 at around 11.00 A.M. the Food Inspector, Koorebhar,
Sultanpur had found the revisionist selling food items i.e. coriander powder, chili powder, turmeric powder and pan masala etc.
He purchased three packets of 60 pouches each of Sanjog Pan Masala from the revisionist for Rs.180/- after disclosing his identity to the revisionist.
The Food Inspector labeled all the packets and forwarded it to Chief Medical Officer, Sultanpur.
The Public Analyst, in his report found that quantity of dissolved base in dilute Hydroelectric Acid was found to be more than .5% from the prescribed norms.
4. The trial court after considering the evidence and the submissions, had convicted and sentenced the revisionist as mentioned above.
Aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, revisionist preferred appeal, which too was dismissed vide impugned judgement and order.
5. The incident is of the year 2001.
More than 18 years have gone by since the samples were taken.
The trial court judgment is dated 29.06.2009.

6. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that the revisionist has undergone three months imprisonment and, he, therefore, submits that his sentence may be reduced to the sentence already undergone.
7.

Considering the fact that the incident had happened 18 years before and also considering the judgement of the Supreme Court rendered in the case of Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562, in which the Supreme Court after considering the age of the appellant in that case and taking into account the fact that the incident was very old, reduced the sentence to the period already undergone, interest of justice would meet if conviction of the accused-applicant is upheld and sentence is reduced to the period already undergone.

entities.text: Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the revision is partly allowed while maintaining the conviction, but the sentence is reduced to the period already undergone.
